display.title: Pesach Is All About Children
display.summary_short: Why Pesach centers on children: the babies Hashem saved in Egypt, the children who first sang at the Red Sea, a Seder built around their questions, and the parade they will lead when Moshiach comes.
display.summary_long: A short pre-Pesach talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that Pesach is different from every other holiday because it centers on children. Pharaoh tried to destroy the Jewish people by throwing the baby boys into the Nile, but Hashem sent angels to catch them and made milk and honey flow from the rocks to nourish them. At the splitting of the Red Sea, those children were the first to recognize Hashem and call out, 'This is my G-d and I will glorify Him.' That is why the Seder is written with children in mind: the Four Questions and the dipping of karpas are there to make them curious, because a person who is too shy to ask never learns. And when Moshiach comes, the children of Tzivos Hashem will lead the great parade out of exile, carried on heavenly clouds to Eretz Yisroel, as the prophet Daniel foretold.
display.lesson: Children play the leading role on Pesach; don't be shy to ask questions, because asking is how we learn.
